provenance_summary: V1-B first expansion wave. Polydopamine (PDA) composites inspired by mussel adhesive proteins, used as universal surface coating for enhanced adsorption of heavy metals and dyes.

mechanisms.description: Mussel-inspired PDA coating: dopamine self-polymerizes under alkaline conditions to form adherent polydopamine film with abundant -OH and -NH₂ groups for metal coordination

pollutant_feature.text: Heavy metal ions and cationic dyes

bio_structure.text: Phenolic -OH and amine -NH₂ groups on PDA

interaction.text: PDA coating provides -OH and -NH₂ groups for coordination and electrostatic interaction

why_it_works.text: Enhanced adsorption capacity vs unmodified substrate

boundary_conditions.text: Use only within the pollutant/material/pH and source context cited for this mechanism.

causal_chain.verification_quote: Dopamine (DA), one kind of mussel-inspired adhesive protein, which can be easily attach onto various substrates firmly by oxidation and self-polymerization to form polydopamine (PDA) coating under basic reaction conditions.

engineering_constraints.description: Dopamine polymerization: 500 mg DA in Tris buffer (pH 8.5), stirred 24h at room temperature

design_translation.idea: Use dopamine self-polymerization to create universal PDA coating on any substrate, providing abundant functional groups for heavy metal and dye adsorption
examples: PDA coating on magnetic GO for recyclable adsorbent
design_translation.applicability: Universal surface functionalization for adsorption, catalysis, and biomedical applications

knowledge_gaps: PDA coating thickness control and optimization
Long-term stability of PDA coating in harsh conditions

narrative.text: Polydopamine (PDA) is a mussel-inspired polymer that can coat virtually any surface under mild alkaline conditions. The catechol and amine groups on PDA provide versatile chemistry for further functionalization and direct pollutant binding.
